newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda seeks bigger mkt share with new mini vehicle.
newsitem.headline: Honda seeks bigger mkt share with new mini vehicle.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd unveiled its first new mini vehicle in four years on Friday, aiming to grab a greater share of Japan's lucrative small-car sector.
Japan's third biggest carmaker said its "Life" 660cc multi-purpose mini vehicle would go on sale in Japanese showrooms on April 27.
The new car is the first completely new Honda car in the popular mini-vehicle category since March 1993.
"We decided to launch a new mini vehicle...given strong consumer demand," Honda president and chief executive officer Nobuhiko Kawamoto told reporters at a media launch for the new car.
The market for recreational and mini vehicles has been booming in Japan as motorists have opted for compact runabouts rather than traditional family sedans.
"We can raise our share with this new model, although we don't know by how much," Riku Iwai, a Honda managing director in charge of domestic car sales, told Reuters.
The Life will sell for a minimum price of 898,000 yen ($7,126) in Japan and Honda aims to sell 8,000 of them a month.

Honda saw its share of Japan's mini-vehicle market fall to 9.6 percent last calendar year from 10.6 percent in 1995, as leading minicar makers Suzuki Motor Corp and Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd boosted their shares with minivan-style multi-purpose vehicles.
Excluding mini vehicles, Honda's share of the domestic market rose to 10 percent in 1996 from 7.5 percent a year earlier, helped by strong demand for its recreational vehicles.

Despite the attractions of the "new model effect", or a surge in orders associated with brand new models, other Japanese car makers have generally been hesitant about introducing new mini vehicles before changes in Japan's vehicle classifications next year.
Japan is set to change its classifications for mini vehicles in October 1998 in order to improve collision safety and allow makers to produce vehicles with longer and wider bodies.
Iwai said Honda would introduce more new mini vehicles after the changes. ($1=126 yen)
